question: Should ClawHub accept a root dependency and skill-install path that require SSH access to a currently private `openclaw/design-system` repository?
rationale: This is an organization/release-access decision rather than a code-shape issue; the diff is coherent, but normal hosted installs and deployment automation cannot prove or consume the dependency until repository access is resolved.

options.title: Wait for public package access
options.body: Keep the PR open and draft until `openclaw/design-system` is public or otherwise installable without special cross-repository credentials.

options.title: Provision explicit credentials
options.body: Allow merge only after CI, deploy, and Dependabot have narrowly scoped read access and fresh-install proof demonstrates the path works.

options.title: Split skills from runtime dependency
options.body: Publish or vendor the agent-skill guidance through a separate path if maintainers want skills before the CSS package is broadly consumable.

recommendation.title: Wait for public package access
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open and draft until `openclaw/design-system` is public or otherwise installable without special cross-repository credentials.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is both the recent owner of the changed dependency/lockfile surface and the collaborator carrying the design-system install stack.
